rotate-hint: Turn your device sideways to get more space.
back-result: For your teacher (or an AI tutor, if you use one)
problems-title: The workshop cannot open this task.
problems-more: Ask the person who gave you the link. Or choose a task from the list above.
fail-wall: There is a wall in front of Kiko. It stands at square ({x}, {y}) and cannot move forward.
fail-not-at-goal: The program has ended, but Kiko is at square ({x}, {y}), not at the goal.
fail-limit: The program does not stop: after {steps} commands it is still not done. Is Kiko going back and forth or round in circles?
fail-empty: Your program has no blocks yet. Attach blocks below “Program”.
fail-too-many-blocks: You used {used} blocks. At most {max} are allowed.
fail-unknown-block: This world does not know the block “{name}”.
fail-unknown-variable: The variable “{name}” has no value yet.
describe-labyrinth: Maze. Kiko is at square ({x}, {y}) and faces {facing}.
problem-not-object: This is not a task in the workshop's format.
problem-unreadable: The link is damaged. The task cannot be read.
problem-too-long: The link is too long (at most {max} characters).
problem-id: The id is made of lower-case letters, digits and hyphens.
problem-text: A text per language belongs here: { "de": …, "en": … }.
problem-language: The workshop does not know this language (de, en).
problem-text-length: The text is empty or longer than {max} characters.
problem-world-type: The workshop does not know this world.
problem-world-version: This version of the world does not exist. The newest is {newest}.
problem-config: The world needs its settings as an object.
problem-facing: The direction is north, east, south or west.
problem-map-size: The map has rows of the same length and at most {max} × {max} squares.
problem-map-chars: The map only contains #, ., S and Z.
problem-map-start: The map needs exactly one start S.
problem-map-goal: The map needs a goal Z.
problem-toolbox: The toolbox is a list of 1 to 30 blocks.
problem-block: There is no block “{name}” in this world.
problem-program: This is not a valid program.
problem-tests: Test cases: at most 9, each with “config” only.
problem-checks: At least one check is needed.
problem-back-url: The way back is a path on lernapps.net, e.g. /informatik/schleifen/.
fail-empty-slot: The block “{block}” still needs a question. Put a question into the gap.
solved-all: Done! Your program solves all {count} puzzles.
tests-explain: This task has {count} puzzles: variants of the maze or picture. Your program has to solve them all. “Run” tries it in each one in turn. Use the tabs above the picture to look at each puzzle.
help-blocks: Drag blocks from the list and hang them under the brown block “Program”. Only blocks that hang there will run. Loose blocks are pale (a screen reader says “disabled”).
help-robot: Kiko is a robot. The triangle on its circle shows where it is looking. “left” and “right” are from Kiko's point of view, so from the triangle.
help-run: “Run” runs your program. “One step” runs just one block. The block that just ran is marked in the work area.
help-keys: With the keyboard: press Tab until you are in the list of blocks. Use the arrow keys to go through the list (in a row, the right arrow). Enter picks a block. Use the arrow keys to choose its place; a screen reader tells you where it goes. Enter puts it down. Press T to go back to the list. To change a number in a block: arrow right to the number, Enter, type the number, Enter.
explain-wiederhole: “repeat … times”: the blocks inside run as many times as the number says. A block that repeats other blocks is called a loop. Change the number by clicking it or with the keyboard.
explain-solange: “while … do”: the blocks inside run again and again as long as the answer to the question is “yes”.
explain-wenn: “if … then”: the blocks inside only run if the answer to the question is “yes”.
explain-wenn-sonst: “if … then … else”: if the answer is “yes”, the blocks at “then” run. If it is “no”, the blocks at “else” run.
explain-nicht: “not” turns the answer to a question around: “yes” becomes “no”.
explain-wand-voraus: “wall ahead?” asks: is there a wall right in front of Kiko?
explain-wand-links: “wall on the left?” asks: is there a wall on Kiko's left?
explain-wand-rechts: “wall on the right?” asks: is there a wall on Kiko's right?
explain-am-ziel: “at the goal?” asks: is Kiko standing on the goal?
help-map-labyrinth: Dark squares are walls, light squares are the path, the green square with the flag is the goal. The dots show where Kiko has been. The numbers at the top are columns, the numbers on the left are rows: square (4, 2) means column 4, row 2.
explain-gehe: “move … pixels”: Kiko moves forward that many pixels and draws a line. Click the number to change it.
explain-drehe-rechts-um: “turn left/right by … degrees”: Kiko turns on the spot. 90 degrees is a quarter turn, 360 degrees is once all the way round.
explain-farbe: “use the colour …”: from now on Kiko draws in this colour. Whether your picture matches the grey one does not depend on the colour.
explain-stift-hoch: “pen up”: Kiko moves without drawing. “pen down”: it draws again.
describe-turtle: Drawing area. Kiko is at ({x}, {y}) and faces {winkel} degrees (0 degrees is up). It has drawn {lines} lines.
describe-turtle-target: The grey picture shows what Kiko should draw.
fail-picture-missing: Your picture is not the same yet: at ({x}, {y}) a piece of the grey line is missing.
fail-picture-extra: At ({x}, {y}) you drew a line that is not in the grey picture.
fail-too-many-lines: Kiko has drawn more than {max} lines. Does your program stop?
problem-turtle-start: The start has x and y from 0 to {size} and an angle from 0 to 359.
help-map-turtle: When drawing, Kiko does not walk over squares: it draws on an area of 200 × 200 pixels. It should copy the grey picture. The numbers on the edge help you find places: (50, 100) means 50 to the right, 100 down. At the start Kiko looks up.
authoring-intro: For teachers and apps: paste a task as JSON. The workshop checks it at once. Then try it out and copy the link.
authoring-schema: The format is in the schema:
authoring-language: The workshop shows the language of the page: a German explainer links the German link (/coding/app/), an English one the English link (/coding/en/app/). Give the texts of the task as { "de": …, "en": … }; German is required.
authoring-script: At build time an app checks its task and model solution with the check script:
authoring-length: Length after c=: {length} of at most {max} characters
problem-json: This is not valid JSON. Is a comma or a bracket missing?
authoring-visit: A link with a task holds for the whole visit. Choosing another task in the list leaves it; the browser’s back button returns to it. So do not add a route (#…) to the link.
problem-number: A number from {min} to {max} is allowed here.
problem-target-lines: The target picture has too many lines (at most {max}) or does not end.
fail-endless: Your program goes round in circles without Kiko doing anything. Look at your loops.
solved-labyrinth: Done! Kiko is at the goal.
describe-labyrinth-around: Free: {free}. The goal is at square ({gx}, {gy}).
copy-missing: Copying does not work here. Select the text and copy it yourself.
problem-solution-block: The model solution uses the block “{name}”, which is not in the toolbox.
solved-both: Done! Your program solves both puzzles.
all-done: That was the last task. You have done all the tasks of the workshop!
scroll-hint: Swipe the row of blocks sideways to see them all.
explain-weg-frei: “way ahead clear?” asks: can Kiko move forward without bumping into a wall?
authoring-beginners: For beginners: “way ahead clear?” is “wall ahead?” turned round and needs no “not”. A command with "locked": true in the start program is fixed: learners only fill its gaps (gap tasks).
fail-predict-no-way: First set Kiko's way: square by square, as Kiko goes.
fail-predict-no-picture: First choose the picture Kiko draws.
fail-predict-step: Your prediction is right up to step {ok}. In step {step} Kiko goes to square ({x}, {y}), you set square ({px}, {py}).
fail-predict-step-first: Step 1 is already different: Kiko goes to square ({x}, {y}), you set square ({px}, {py}).
fail-predict-more: Your prediction is right up to step {ok}. Then Kiko goes on: in step {step} it goes to square ({x}, {y}).
fail-predict-less: Your prediction is right up to step {ok}. Then Kiko stops at square ({x}, {y}). After that you set square ({px}, {py}).
fail-predict-line: Your picture is right up to line {ok}. Kiko draws line {line} from ({x1}, {y1}) to ({x2}, {y2}), in your picture it goes to ({px}, {py}).
fail-predict-line-first: Line 1 is already different: Kiko draws it from ({x1}, {y1}) to ({x2}, {y2}), in your picture it goes to ({px}, {py}).
fail-predict-line-more: Your picture is right up to line {ok}. Then Kiko draws line {line} as well: from ({x1}, {y1}) to ({x2}, {y2}).
fail-predict-line-less: Kiko draws only {lines} lines. Your picture has more.
problem-predict-field: “vorhersage” exists only with the check “vorhersage”, and only in the world turtle.
problem-predict-checks: With “vorhersage” it is the only check.
problem-predict-start: A prediction needs a start program with blocks: it is the program learners read.
problem-predict-pictures: Turtle: “vorhersage” is { "bilder": [ … ] } with 2 or 3 programs for the wrong pictures.
problem-predict-run: Puzzle {n}: the start program does not run to its end. A prediction needs a run without errors.
problem-predict-same: Puzzle {n}: this wrong picture is the same as the right one.
predict-from-start: Kiko starts at {field}. Which square does it go to first?
predict-from: Last set: {field}. Which square does Kiko go to next?
predict-next: Next square, as seen on the map
phase-predict: Read the program and set Kiko's way. Then press “Run”: Kiko sets off, and you see whether you were right.
phase-predict-picture: Read the program and choose the picture Kiko draws. Then press “Run”.
help-predict-read: The program is ready. You can read it but not change it. Below the blocks it is written as text, too.
help-predict-way: Set the squares Kiko goes through, one after the other: click a square next to the last one, or use the arrow buttons. The arrows are for the map (up is up), not for where Kiko looks. A step is a new square; turning is not a step.
help-predict-run: “Run” lets Kiko carry out the program. Then you see whether your prediction is right, and if not, at which step it differs. Then you change it and try again.
tests-explain-predict: This task has {count} puzzles: versions of the maze or picture, with the same program. Predict for each puzzle what Kiko does. “Run” compares them all, one after the other.
solved-predict: Well predicted! Kiko does exactly what you said.
help-predict-picture: Below the sheet there are several pictures. Kiko draws only one of them with this program. Choose it. Each picture has a description, line by line.
help-map-turtle-predict: When drawing, Kiko does not move over squares: it draws on a sheet of 200 × 200 pixels. The numbers at the edge help you find places: (50, 100) means 50 to the right, 100 down. At the start Kiko stands in the middle and looks up.
